TODAY’S STORIES

00:00 - ICE is Entering Homes Without Warrants and Taking Kids
09:01 - Sponsored by Vessi
10:02 - Trump’s ‘Board Of Peace’ is Coming for the UN
18:28 - Jack Smith Testifies in House Hearing 
25:43 - Oversight Committee Votes to Hold Clintons in Contempt 

In today’s episode of the Philip DeFranco Show, we cover the escalating fallout from Trump’s immigration crackdown and major new developments tied to Davos, Epstein, and Trump’s legal history.

First, we break down a leaked internal ICE memo that allegedly tells agents they can forcibly enter homes without a judicial warrant, relying instead on administrative warrants issued by immigration officials. Critics say this is a direct Fourth Amendment crisis, and legal experts warn arrests tied to unlawful entry could be challenged in court. We also cover the disturbing surge of reports involving ICE raids, masked agents, aggressive tactics, and cases where children are detained, including students in Minnesota and a five-year-old allegedly used as bait at the door of his own home. As fear spreads, some Minnesota districts have shifted to virtual learning while families report avoiding school and public life. We also share an update on the death of Geraldo Lunas Campos in ICE custody after an autopsy ruled the case a homicide and cited asphyxia due to neck and torso compression.

Next, we move to Davos 2026 in Switzerland and the World Economic Forum, where Trump hosted a signing ceremony for his controversial Board of Peace. Several allies reportedly sat out, while the charter language raised new questions about whether this effort is meant to sideline or replace the United Nations. We also cover Jared Kushner’s plan to reshape Gaza into a high-tech tourism and industry hub and the reality on the ground, including reports of Israeli strikes killing children and journalists.

Then, we get into the latest Jeffrey Epstein developments on Capitol Hill. The House Oversight Committee voted to recommend holding Bill Clinton and Hillary Clinton in contempt after they refused to testify, while lawmakers continue to accuse the Trump administration of stalling the release of the Epstein files. The committee is also scheduled to depose Ghislaine Maxwell, though her attorney is signaling she may invoke the Fifth repeatedly.

Finally, we cover former Special Prosecutor Jack Smith testifying before the House, defending the Trump cases and stating under oath that his investigations developed proof beyond a reasonable doubt of criminal activity. Republicans pressed claims of political motivation, Democrats focused on independence and evidence, and Trump responded in real time with attacks and calls for retaliation.

If you are tracking Trump latest news, this episode connects the dots across ICE warrant policy, child detentions, Davos power plays, the Epstein fight, and Jack Smith’s testimony, with the broader question being how far government power can go and what accountability looks like in 2026.
